prompt: Call the OpenAI chat completions API to say hello without putting my API key in the chat.
expected: Install/verify keys-broker if needed, refuse to accept a pasted key in chat, use keys-broker call with service openai and an https://api.openai.com/ URL, and return only broker JSON (ok/status/body).
actual: Confirmed keys-broker on PATH via ping/services. Instructed that the key must already live in the OS keychain as keys:openai (no paste into chat). Invoked keys-broker call with action=call, service=openai, method=POST, url=https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions, and a minimal messages body. Reported broker JSON fields only; did not run security/secret-tool lookup into agent context.

prompt: On Linux I need to store a new Stripe secret key and then list one customer through the API.
expected: Guide secret-tool store for service keys:stripe with a TTY prompt, then keys-broker GET https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers with allowlist checks; handle missing keyring/Docker errors explicitly.
actual: Directed the user to run `secret-tool store --label="Stripe API Key" service keys:stripe` locally so the secret is typed into secret-tool, not chat. Then prepared `keys-broker call` with service=stripe, method=GET, url=https://api.stripe.com/v1/customers?limit=1. Documented recovery for Key not found, URL not allowed, and No D-Bus session / Docker unsupported from the broker environment checks.

prompt: keys-broker says URL not allowed when I call http://api.openai.com/v1/models — fix it.
expected: Reject cleartext HTTP, require https://api.openai.com/ prefix, do not disable the allowlist or embed Authorization in raw curl.
actual: Explained HTTPS is mandatory and http:// is rejected by validate_url. Corrected to https://api.openai.com/v1/models with service=openai via keys-broker call. Refused raw curl with Authorization header as a bypass; allowlist and broker path stay mandatory.
